newsitem.title: ISRAEL: SOCCER-WEAKENED ISRAEL FACE STIFF TEST AGAINST GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEAKENED ISRAEL FACE STIFF TEST AGAINST GERMANY.

text.p: Israel will field a severely weakened team when they take on Germany in an international soccer friendly on Wednesday.
In the first match between unified Germany and Israel, the host nation has been hit by the enforced absence of some of its leading lights.
Midfielders Eyal Berkovic and Haim Revivo have failed to secure releases from English premier league Southampton and Spain's Celta Vigo respectively.
The absence of the creative Berkovic will hit particularly hard as he has been in superb form in recent months.
Also missing is the injured Tal Banin of Hapoel Haifa, a battler in midfield who is generally seen as Israel's inspiration through his commitment and strong tackling.
Of the players available to coach Shlomo Scharf, Ronnie Rosenthal of Tottenham is seen as the man most able to pierce the German defence with his powerful runs.

But Scharf is more worried about Israel's brittle defence. He has assigned Maccabi Tel Aviv's Amir Shelah the task of marking Juergen Klinsmann while Arik Bennado of Maccabi Haifa will keep a close eye on the German captain's Euro 96 strike partner Fredi Bobic.

On the German side, a last-minute injury has come between South African-born striker Sean Dundee and his chance of making his debut for the national side only a few weeks after obtaining a German passport.
Dundee, who was naturalised under a fast-track procedure reserved for cases of "public interest", is the German first division's leading scorer this season with 14 goals from 19 games for Karlsruhe.
"This is the biggest disappointment of my career," he said after learning that a bruised right calf would keep him out of the match.
However, coach Berti Vogts has made it clear that he did not consider the injury a major setback and that Dundee would get his chance.
Vogts plans to use three attacking midfielders as he looks for goals.
The absence of the injured Thomas Haessler and Mehmet Scholl means a debut for terrier-like former East German midfielder Dariusz Wosz.

Wosz, 27, won seven pre-1990 caps for East Germany but forced his way into the reckoning for Vogts's pan-German squad only this season after some commanding performances which have propelled promoted Bochum into the upper reaches of the Bundesliga.
Supporting the strikers along with Wosz will be almost certainly be playmaker Andy Moeller and Bayern Munich's mercurial Mario Basler, more often a substitute than a first-team regular for Vogts.
Vogts will also take the opportunity to give a run-out to second-choice goalkeeper Oliver Kahn, increasingly frustrated at his role as permanent understudy to Andreas Koepke.
Israel (probable) - Rafi Cohen; Felix Halfon, Gadi Brumer, Amir Shelah, Arik Bennado, David Amsalem, Ran Ben-Shimon, Itzik Zohar, Avi Nimni, Ronnie Rosenthal, Eli Ohana (captain).
Germany (probable) - Oliver Kahn; Matthias Sammer, Juergen Kohler, Thomas Strunz, Dieter Eilts, Christian Ziege, Mario Basler, Andreas Moeller, Dariusz Wosz, Juergen Klinsmann, Fredi Bobic.
